steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Semiotics: the study of signs and symbols — everything on stage is a sign that carries meaning.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Denotation: what something literally is; connotation: what it suggests or symbolises. A red light denotes light colour but connotes danger, passion or hell.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Proxemics: the spatial relationship between characters — distance shows relationship, power or tension.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Blocking: the precise movement and positioning of actors on stage — every position is deliberate.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain the difference between denotation and connotation, using a specific example from a production you have seen. | How does a director use proxemics and levels to communicate the relationship between two characters? | Describe how semiotics helps an audience understand the deeper meaning of a performance.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Denotation is the literal meaning; connotation is the associated meaning. E.g. a wedding dress denotes a bride's clothing but connotes purity, commitment, social expectation. steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Use stage position abbreviations (USR, CS, DS) to show precise knowledge Always explain what a staging choice CONNOTES, not just what it looks like Proxemics questions need specific distance examples — 'standing close' is vague Semiotics = everything is a sign. Ask yourself: what does this choice symbolise?
